\begin{CRchronicle}{28}
Reed came on and the reeds went into the beds as the seed had, judged by the arm, never by a figure. The hands that cut them went uncounted. The yard went around the clean dark line, the grey named the thaw, and the place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come back: a look, a wide step, no number. Sella Vail sent the woman who asked what the reeds cost to the pot --- \emph{the house has said it} --- and carried the boy at the half-pace. One hundred and twenty-three days old, he read the going-around as a chart closed over a note nobody had opened: exact, complete, worth nothing.

Under the roof the shelf kept its two unnamed gaps in a room the fold did not touch, its one crust and its empty place, and no third came. Sella told the fire it was the thaw and said \emph{The house will keep it}. Men came before first grey into the back room; Jorra Vail gave them no name, came through with grey dust ground into both forearms and told a pot \emph{You’ll do}. His bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence. Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed; his seventh year stood held, six years in a worn thumb-mark and the seventh where the house could not check it, and his stroke went on without the half-check.

That evening Tarn brought the sentence to the threshold of the word that would call the loan --- that an ear is worth more than a debt --- and stopped there: no figure, no name, the loan uncalled. His held breath stayed unspent. The boy filed the stopped sentence on the interval tray, an interval and not a payment. A reed-cutter’s tally went past in a grey cord --- \emph{You can ask the cord}; \emph{No more can the Court} --- its knots unread. Orra Weir gave a date for a figure, Mira Silt answered a thin run with \emph{Ask the river}, and the clerk sat for a measure nobody called while the market sold over him. Berr Clay read one in twelve and took himself out of his sentence with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}.

That evening Sella set him on his bed, put the fold right, left the thread frozen, told the fire it was the thaw and went to her own bed. The door stood a finger’s width open: the river’s note came through the gap, the fire missed its fifth breath, and the boards kept a knot. Three counts in three places; none became one. He turned out his file and found every object in its place --- six hearings with no seventh, three answers unpaid, the near-saying on the tray. Nobody said he was a hundred and twenty-five days old. His small hand went up an inch toward the water and came down; the count went on, unspent and spoken by nobody.
\end{CRchronicle}
